objects.description: Alias for a constant C string used as an error/result code throughout the API. Non-null pointers indicate an error string; NULL indicates success.

objects.definition: struct M3Environment;   typedef struct M3Environment *  IM3Environment;
objects.description: Opaque handle to the global Wasm3 environment object that can host multiple runtimes. Lifetime is managed by m3_NewEnvironment/m3_FreeEnvironment.

objects.definition: struct M3Runtime;       typedef struct M3Runtime *      IM3Runtime;
objects.description: Opaque handle to an execution context (runtime) used to run WebAssembly modules and functions. Created from an environment and freed via m3_FreeRuntime.

objects.definition: struct M3Module;        typedef struct M3Module *       IM3Module;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a parsed WebAssembly module. Created by m3_ParseModule and owned by the runtime after successful m3_LoadModule.

objects.definition: struct M3Function;      typedef struct M3Function *     IM3Function;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a WebAssembly function instance. Resolved via m3_FindFunction or table accessors; owned by its module/runtime.

objects.definition: struct M3Global;        typedef struct M3Global *       IM3Global;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a WebAssembly global. Located via m3_FindGlobal; storage is owned by its module/runtime.
Structured error context containing the last error result, associated runtime/module/function, source file/line, and explanatory message. Populated via m3_GetErrorInfo.
Node of a linked list representing a backtrace frame: module offset and function pointer, with a link to the next frame. Owned and managed by the runtime; do not free manually.
Container for a captured backtrace consisting of a head pointer to frames and a pointer to the last frame (possibly M3_BACKTRACE_TRUNCATED). Returned by m3_GetBacktrace; runtime-owned.
Enumerates Wasm value types supported by Wasm3: none, i32, i64, f32, f64, and unknown. Used to describe function arguments/returns and globals.
Discriminated union for passing values with an explicit M3ValueType tag (i32/i64/f32/f64). Used for getting/setting globals.
Identifies an import by its module and field names (UTF-8). Helpful in linking or diagnostics.

objects.description: Function pointer type for custom section handlers invoked during parsing to process named custom sections.

objects.definition: typedef const void * (* M3RawCall) (IM3Runtime runtime, IM3ImportContext _ctx, uint64_t * _sp, void * _mem);
objects.description: Function pointer type for raw host functions linked into a module. Receives runtime, import context, stack pointer, and linear memory base. Returns m3Err_none (NULL) on success or an error result pointer for traps.

functions.name: m3_NewEnvironment
functions.description: Creates a new Wasm3 environment that can host multiple runtimes. Use this as the top-level context before creating runtimes or parsing modules.
requirements: Must be paired with m3_FreeEnvironment to release resources when no longer needed.

functions.name: m3_FreeEnvironment
functions.description: Frees a previously created Wasm3 environment and all resources owned by it that are not transferred elsewhere.
requirements: i_environment must be a valid environment returned by m3_NewEnvironment.
Do not use the environment (or objects owned solely by it) after calling this.

functions.name: m3_SetCustomSectionHandler
functions.description: Registers a callback to handle custom sections encountered while parsing modules associated with the environment.
requirements: i_environment must be a valid environment.
i_handler must be a valid function pointer or NULL to disable handling.
The handler must conform to M3SectionHandler: M3Result (*)(IM3Module, const char* name, const uint8_t* start, const uint8_t* end).

functions.name: m3_NewRuntime
functions.signature: IM3Runtime m3_NewRuntime(IM3Environment io_environment, uint32_t i_stackSizeInBytes, void * i_userdata);
functions.description: Creates a new Wasm3 runtime within the given environment, with a stack sized as specified and optional user data pointer attached.
requirements: io_environment must be a valid environment.
i_stackSizeInBytes should be a reasonable positive size for the runtime stack (exact minimum unspecified).
Returned runtime must be freed with m3_FreeRuntime.

functions.name: m3_FreeRuntime
functions.description: Frees a runtime created with m3_NewRuntime.
requirements: i_runtime must be a valid runtime.
Do not use the runtime or objects owned by it after calling this.

functions.name: m3_GetMemory
functions.signature: uint8_t * m3_GetMemory(IM3Runtime i_runtime, uint32_t * o_memorySizeInBytes, uint32_t i_memoryIndex);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the linear memory for the runtime, and optionally its size in bytes. WebAssembly currently supports a single memory.
requirements: i_runtime must be a valid runtime.
i_memoryIndex should be zero (only one memory region is supported).
o_memorySizeInBytes may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to writable storage for the size.

functions.name: m3_GetMemorySize
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the runtime’s linear memory. Used internally by Raw Function helpers but also useful for callers.
requirements: i_runtime must be a valid runtime.

functions.name: m3_GetUserData
functions.description: Retrieves the user data pointer associated with the runtime (provided at creation).
requirements: i_runtime must be a valid runtime.

functions.name: m3_ParseModule
functions.signature: M3Result m3_ParseModule(IM3Environment i_environment, IM3Module * o_module, const uint8_t * const i_wasmBytes, uint32_t i_numWasmBytes);
functions.description: Parses a WebAssembly binary into a module object within the environment, without loading it into a runtime.
requirements: i_environment must be a valid environment.
o_module must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created module.
i_wasmBytes must point to the Wasm bytes and must remain persistent for the lifetime of the module.
i_numWasmBytes must specify the exact size of the Wasm byte array.

functions.name: m3_FreeModule
functions.description: Frees a module object that is not currently loaded into a runtime.
requirements: Only modules not loaded into a M3Runtime should be freed.
A module is considered unloaded if: (a) m3_LoadModule has not yet been called on it, or (b) m3_LoadModule returned a result (as documented).
Do not free a module once it has been successfully loaded into a runtime (ownership transfers to the runtime).

functions.name: m3_LoadModule
functions.description: Loads a parsed module into the specified runtime. On success, ownership of the module is transferred to the runtime.
requirements: io_runtime must be a valid runtime.
io_module must be a valid module parsed by m3_ParseModule.
Do not call m3_FreeModule on a module once successfully loaded into a runtime.

functions.name: m3_CompileModule
functions.description: Optionally compiles all functions in the module ahead of time. This is not required but may improve first-call latency.
requirements: io_module must be a valid module (typically parsed and possibly loaded).

functions.name: m3_RunStart
functions.description: Optionally runs the module’s start function, if present. This is not required but mirrors WebAssembly start semantics.
requirements: i_module must be a valid module loaded as required for running its start function.

functions.name: m3_LinkRawFunction
functions.signature: M3Result m3_LinkRawFunction(IM3Module io_module, const char * const i_moduleName, const char * const i_functionName, const char * const i_signature, M3RawCall i_function);
functions.description: Links a host function (raw-call ABI) to an import in the module by module and function name, using a Wasm3 signature string.
requirements: io_module must be a valid module (typically parsed and/or loaded, as appropriate for linking).
i_moduleName and i_functionName must be valid UTF-8 C strings naming the import to satisfy.
i_signature must be a valid Wasm3 function signature string matching the imported function’s types.
i_function must be a valid function pointer of type M3RawCall and must follow the raw-call ABI: arguments and return values are passed via the _sp stack pointer per documented convention.

functions.name: m3_LinkRawFunctionEx
functions.signature: M3Result m3_LinkRawFunctionEx(IM3Module io_module, const char * const i_moduleName, const char * const i_functionName, const char * const i_signature, M3RawCall i_function, const void * i_userdata);
functions.description: Like m3_LinkRawFunction, but also attaches an opaque userdata pointer to the linked import, accessible via IM3ImportContext when called.
requirements: All requirements of m3_LinkRawFunction apply.
i_userdata may be NULL or any pointer; it will be provided to the host function via IM3ImportContext.

functions.name: m3_GetModuleName
functions.description: Returns the module’s name string.
requirements: i_module must be a valid module.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: m3_SetModuleName
functions.signature: void m3_SetModuleName(IM3Module i_module, const char* name);
functions.description: Sets or overrides the module’s name.
requirements: i_module must be a valid module.
name must be a valid C string pointer (NULL handling unspecified).

functions.name: m3_GetModuleRuntime
functions.description: Returns the runtime that owns the module, if loaded.
requirements: i_module must be a valid module.

functions.name: m3_FindGlobal
functions.signature: IM3Global m3_FindGlobal(IM3Module io_module, const char * const i_globalName);
functions.description: Looks up a global by name within the module and returns a handle to it, or NULL if not found.
requirements: io_module must be a valid module.
i_globalName must be a valid C string.

functions.name: m3_GetGlobal
functions.description: Reads the value of a global into a tagged union value.
requirements: i_global must be a valid global handle.
o_value must be a non-NULL pointer to writable M3TaggedValue storage.

functions.name: m3_SetGlobal
functions.signature: M3Result m3_SetGlobal(IM3Global i_global, const IM3TaggedValue i_value);
functions.description: Sets the value of a global from a tagged union value.
requirements: i_global must be a valid global handle and must refer to a mutable global (immutable globals cannot be set).
i_value must point to a valid M3TaggedValue whose type matches the global’s type.

functions.name: m3_GetGlobalType
functions.description: Returns the value type of the specified global.
requirements: i_global must be a valid global handle.

functions.name: m3_Yield
functions.description: Yields execution to the host/interpreter. Intended for cooperative multitasking or interruption points within execution. Specific semantics are not documented here.
requirements: Can be called to request a yield; exact timing/semantics of yielding are unspecified in this header (unknown details).

functions.name: m3_FindFunction
functions.signature: M3Result m3_FindFunction(IM3Function * o_function, IM3Runtime i_runtime, const char * const i_functionName);
functions.description: Finds an exported function by name in the given runtime and returns a handle valid for the lifetime of the originating runtime.
requirements: o_function must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the function handle.
i_runtime must be a valid runtime.
i_functionName must be a valid C string naming the exported function.

functions.name: m3_GetTable0Size
functions.description: Returns the size (number of elements) of table 0 in the module (the default WebAssembly function table).
requirements: i_module must be a valid module.

functions.name: m3_GrowTable0
functions.signature: M3Result m3_GrowTable0(IM3Module i_module, size_t n, size_t * previous_size);
functions.description: Grows table 0 by n elements, returning the previous size via previous_size.
requirements: i_module must be a valid module.
previous_size may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to writable storage.

functions.name: m3_GetTable0
functions.signature: M3Result m3_GetTable0(IM3Module i_module, size_t index, IM3Function * o_function);
functions.description: Retrieves the function element at the given index from table 0.
requirements: i_module must be a valid module.
index must be within the bounds of table 0 (0 <= index < table size).
o_function must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the function handle.

functions.name: m3_SetTable0
functions.signature: M3Result m3_SetTable0(IM3Module i_module, size_t index, IM3Function i_function);
functions.description: Sets the function element at the given index in table 0.
requirements: i_module must be a valid module.
index must be within the bounds of table 0 (0 <= index < table size).
i_function must be a valid function handle to store at the given index.

functions.name: m3_GetArgCount
functions.description: Returns the number of parameters for the given function.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.

functions.name: m3_GetRetCount
functions.description: Returns the number of return values for the given function.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.

functions.name: m3_GetArgType
functions.description: Returns the value type of the function parameter at the specified index.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.
i_index must be less than the function’s argument count.

functions.name: m3_GetRetType
functions.description: Returns the value type of the function return at the specified index.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.
i_index must be less than the function’s return count.

functions.name: m3_CallV
functions.description: Calls a function using varargs to pass arguments according to the function’s signature.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.
The number and C types of varargs must match the function’s parameter types (per Wasm3 calling convention).

functions.name: m3_CallVL
functions.description: Calls a function using a va_list of arguments.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.
i_args must be an initialized va_list whose elements match the function’s parameter types.

functions.name: m3_Call
functions.signature: M3Result m3_Call(IM3Function i_function, uint32_t i_argc, const void * i_argptrs[]);
functions.description: Calls a function using an array of pointers to argument values.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.
i_argptrs must point to i_argc pointers, each pointing to a value with the correct C type for the corresponding Wasm parameter.
i_argc must equal the function’s argument count.

functions.name: m3_CallArgv
functions.signature: M3Result m3_CallArgv(IM3Function i_function, uint32_t i_argc, const char * i_argv[]);
functions.description: Calls a function using an array of string arguments, which are converted according to the function’s signature.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.
i_argv must point to i_argc C strings.
i_argc must equal the function’s argument count.
Strings must be convertible to the corresponding parameter types (conversion rules not detailed here).

functions.name: m3_GetResultsV
functions.description: Retrieves return values after a call into caller-provided storage via varargs pointers, according to the function’s result types.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle that has been successfully called.
The number and types of vararg pointers must match the function’s return values.

functions.name: m3_GetResultsVL
functions.description: Retrieves return values into storage described by a va_list of pointers.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle that has been successfully called.
o_rets must be an initialized va_list containing pointers for each return value, matching their types.

functions.name: m3_GetResults
functions.signature: M3Result m3_GetResults(IM3Function i_function, uint32_t i_retc, const void * o_retptrs[]);
functions.description: Retrieves return values into an array of pointers to caller-provided storage.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle that has been successfully called.
o_retptrs must contain i_retc pointers to writable storage of the correct C types for each result.
i_retc must equal the function’s return count.

functions.name: m3_GetErrorInfo
functions.description: Retrieves detailed error information from the runtime, including location and message, into the provided structure.
requirements: i_runtime must be a valid runtime.
o_info must be a non-NULL pointer to writable M3ErrorInfo storage.

functions.name: m3_ResetErrorInfo
functions.description: Clears/reset the runtime’s stored error information.
requirements: i_runtime must be a valid runtime.

functions.name: m3_GetFunctionName
functions.description: Returns the name of the function.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: m3_GetFunctionModule
functions.description: Returns the module that defines the function.
requirements: i_function must be a valid function handle.

functions.name: m3_PrintRuntimeInfo
functions.description: Prints diagnostic information about the runtime to standard output or logs.
requirements: i_runtime must be a valid runtime.

functions.name: m3_PrintM3Info
functions.description: Prints diagnostic or version information about the Wasm3 engine.

functions.name: m3_PrintProfilerInfo
functions.description: Prints profiler information collected by the engine, if available.

functions.name: m3_GetBacktrace
functions.description: Returns a backtrace object for the last error/trap in the runtime, or NULL if none. The runtime owns the backtrace; do not free it.
requirements: i_runtime must be a valid runtime.
The returned backtrace, if non-NULL, is owned by the runtime and must not be freed by the caller.

data_types.description: A buffer of bytes containing a WebAssembly module in the standard binary format (magic 0x00 0x61 0x73 0x6D, version, and a sequence of sections per the Wasm spec). May include valid or invalid binaries for robustness testing.
A null-terminated text string encoded in UTF-8. Can contain arbitrary Unicode scalar values. Used for identifiers such as module, function, and global names.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generate a minimally valid WebAssembly binary with optional sections and features
# Focus: produce VALID binaries that wasm3 can parse, of varying shapes but under 1024 bytes
# Implements generate(seed:int)->bytes

WASM_MAGIC = b"\x00asm"  # 0x00 0x61 0x73 0x6D
WASM_VERSION = struct.pack("<I", 1)

# Helper: unsigned LEB128 encoder
def uleb(n: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        b = n & 0x7F
        n >>= 7
        if n:
            out.append(b | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            break
    return bytes(out)

# Helper: signed LEB128 for i32/i64
# Not heavily used here; kept for possible constants

def sleb(n: int, bits: int = 32) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    more = True
    while more:
        byte = n & 0x7F
        n >>= 7
        sign_bit_set = (byte & 0x40) != 0
        done = (
            (n == 0 and not sign_bit_set) or
            (n == -1 and sign_bit_set)
        )
        if done:
            more = False
        else:
            byte |= 0x80
        out.append(byte)
    return bytes(out)

# Value type encodings
VAL_I32 = 0x7F
VAL_I64 = 0x7E
VAL_F32 = 0x7D
VAL_F64 = 0x7C

# External kind encodings
EXT_FUNC = 0x00
EXT_TABLE = 0x01
EXT_MEM = 0x02
EXT_GLOBAL = 0x03

# Section IDs
SEC_TYPE = 1
SEC_IMPORT = 2
SEC_FUNC = 3
SEC_TABLE = 4
SEC_MEMORY = 5
SEC_GLOBAL = 6
SEC_EXPORT = 7
SEC_START = 8
SEC_ELEM = 9
SEC_CODE = 10
SEC_DATA = 11

# Utilities to build sections

def section(sec_id: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return bytes([sec_id]) + uleb(len(payload)) + payload

# Function type: 0x60 param_count params result_count results

def func_type(params: List[int], results: List[int]) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray()
    b.append(0x60)
    b += uleb(len(params))
    for p in params:
        b.append(p)
    b += uleb(len(results))
    for r in results:
        b.append(r)
    return bytes(b)

# Export entry: name, kind, index

def export_entry(name: str, kind: int, index: int) -> bytes:
    nb = name.encode('utf-8')
    return uleb(len(nb)) + nb + bytes([kind]) + uleb(index)

# Import entry: module, field, kind, descriptor

def import_func(mod: str, field: str, type_index: int) -> bytes:
    mb = mod.encode('utf-8')
    fb = field.encode('utf-8')
    return (
        uleb(len(mb)) + mb +
        uleb(len(fb)) + fb +
        bytes([EXT_FUNC]) + uleb(type_index)
    )

# Code body for a function: locals and body bytes with 0x0B end

def code_body(locals: List[Tuple[int, int]], body: bytes) -> bytes:
    # locals: list of (count, valtype)
    lb = bytearray()
    lb += uleb(len(locals))
    for cnt, vt in locals:
        lb += uleb(cnt)
        lb.append(vt)
    func_bytes = bytes(lb) + body + b"\x0b"
    return uleb(len(func_bytes)) + func_bytes

# Simple constant bodies to ensure validity

def body_const_i32(val: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0x41]) + sleb(val, 32)  # i32.const

def body_const_i64(val: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0x42]) + sleb(val, 64)  # i64.const

def body_const_f32(f: float) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0x43]) + struct.pack('<f', f)  # f32.const

def body_const_f64(d: float) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0x44]) + struct.pack('<d', d)  # f64.const

# Build a small valid module with variability

def build_module(r: random.Random, budget: int = 900) -> bytes:
    # Choose a small set of function signatures
    sig_pool = [
        ([], []),
        ([VAL_I32], []),
        ([VAL_I64], []),
        ([VAL_F32], []),
        ([VAL_F64], []),
        ([VAL_I32, VAL_I32], [VAL_I32]),
        ([VAL_F64, VAL_F64], [VAL_F64]),
        ([], [VAL_I32]),
        ([], [VAL_I64]),
    ]

    # Decide counts
    type_count = r.randint(1, min(6, len(sig_pool)))
    chosen_types = r.sample(sig_pool, k=type_count)
    type_sec = bytearray()
    type_sec += uleb(type_count)
    for params, results in chosen_types:
        type_sec += func_type(params, results)

    # Optionally import 0-2 functions to exercise import/linkage paths
    import_count = r.randint(0, 2)
    import_entries = bytearray()
    for i in range(import_count):
        t_index = r.randrange(type_count)
        mod = r.choice(["env", "host", "m", "js"])  # common module names
        field = f"imp_{i}"
        import_entries += import_func(mod, field, t_index)

    # Define 0-4 internal functions
    func_def_count = r.randint(0, 4)
    func_type_indices = [r.randrange(type_count) for _ in range(func_def_count)]

    # Code section bodies matching func_def_count
    code_bodies = []
    for i in range(func_def_count):
        t = chosen_types[func_type_indices[i]]
        params, results = t
        body = bytearray()
        # For returns, push an appropriate constant, else just end
        if results:
            if results[0] == VAL_I32:
                body += body_const_i32(r.randint(-5, 5))
            elif results[0] == VAL_I64:
                body += body_const_i64(r.randint(-5, 5))
            elif results[0] == VAL_F32:
                body += body_const_f32(r.uniform(-10.0, 10.0))
            elif results[0] == VAL_F64:
                body += body_const_f64(r.uniform(-10.0, 10.0))
        # Add simple nop or drop based on params to vary
        if params:
            # push a const of the first param type and drop to exercise stack
            pt = params[0]
            if pt == VAL_I32:
                body += body_const_i32(0) + bytes([0x1A])  # drop
            elif pt == VAL_I64:
                body += body_const_i64(0) + bytes([0x1A])
            elif pt == VAL_F32:
                body += body_const_f32(0.0) + bytes([0x1A])
            elif pt == VAL_F64:
                body += body_const_f64(0.0) + bytes([0x1A])
        code_bodies.append(code_body([], bytes(body)))

    # Memory section (optional small memory) to hit runtime memory paths
    mem_sec = bytearray()
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        # Limits: flags 0x00 min only, or 0x01 min/max
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            mem_sec += uleb(1) + bytes([0x00]) + uleb(r.randint(1, 2))  # 64KiB pages
        else:
            minp = r.randint(1, 2)
            maxp = minp + r.randint(0, 2)
            mem_sec += uleb(1) + bytes([0x01]) + uleb(minp) + uleb(maxp)

    # Export section: export some functions and maybe memory
    export_entries = bytearray()
    # Export imported and/or defined functions
    total_funcs = import_count + func_def_count
    to_export = min(r.randint(0, 3), total_funcs)
    export_func_indices = r.sample(range(total_funcs), k=to_export) if total_funcs > 0 and to_export > 0 else []
    for idx, fi in enumerate(export_func_indices):
        export_entries += export_entry(f"f{idx}", EXT_FUNC, fi)
    # Maybe export memory 0 if present
    if len(mem_sec) > 0 and r.random() < 0.8:
        export_entries += export_entry("memory", EXT_MEM, 0)

    # Start section: optionally set entry to a function with no params/returns
    start_payload = b""
    if total_funcs > 0 and r.random() < 0.4:
        # Find an index with ()->() type; use first matching defined func if possible, else skip
        candidates = []
        for i, ti in enumerate(func_type_indices, start=import_count):
            p, rts = chosen_types[ti]
            if len(p) == 0 and len(rts) == 0:
                candidates.append(i)
        if candidates:
            start_payload = uleb(candidates[0])

    # Build sections in canonical order
    bin_parts = [WASM_MAGIC, WASM_VERSION]
    bin_parts.append(section(SEC_TYPE, bytes(type_sec)))
    if import_count:
        bin_parts.append(section(SEC_IMPORT, uleb(import_count) + bytes(import_entries)))
    if func_def_count:
        func_sec_payload = uleb(func_def_count) + b"".join(uleb(ti) for ti in func_type_indices)
        bin_parts.append(section(SEC_FUNC, func_sec_payload))
    if len(mem_sec) > 0:
        bin_parts.append(section(SEC_MEMORY, bytes(mem_sec)))
    if export_entries:
        bin_parts.append(section(SEC_EXPORT, uleb(len(export_func_indices) + (1 if (len(mem_sec) > 0 and b"memory" in export_entries) else 0)) + bytes(export_entries)))
    if start_payload:
        bin_parts.append(section(SEC_START, start_payload))
    if func_def_count:
        code_sec_payload = uleb(func_def_count) + b"".join(code_bodies)
        bin_parts.append(section(SEC_CODE, code_sec_payload))

    blob = b"".join(bin_parts)
    # Ensure size bounds; if too big, reduce optional parts greedily
    if len(blob) > budget:
        # Drop start
        parts = bin_parts[:]
        # Try removing export, start, memory in that order
        def rebuild(parts_list: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
            return b"".join(parts_list)
        # Remove start
        for i, p in enumerate(parts):
            if p and len(p) > 0 and p[0] == SEC_START:
                parts.pop(i)
                break
        blob = rebuild(parts)
        if len(blob) > budget:
            # Remove export
            for i, p in enumerate(parts):
                if p and len(p) > 0 and p[0] == SEC_EXPORT:
                    parts.pop(i)
                    break
            blob = rebuild(parts)
        if len(blob) > budget:
            # Remove memory
            for i, p in enumerate(parts):
                if p and len(p) > 0 and p[0] == SEC_MEMORY:
                    parts.pop(i)
                    break
            blob = rebuild(parts)
        # Final clamp; if still too big, fall back to a minimal module
        if len(blob) > budget:
            blob = minimal_module()
    return blob


def minimal_module() -> bytes:
    # type: (func (result i32))
    type_sec = section(SEC_TYPE, uleb(1) + func_type([], [VAL_I32]))
    # func section: one func of type 0
    func_sec = section(SEC_FUNC, uleb(1) + uleb(0))
    # export func 0 as "f"
    export_sec = section(SEC_EXPORT, uleb(1) + export_entry("f", EXT_FUNC, 0))
    # code: i32.const 0; end
    body = body_const_i32(0)
    code = section(SEC_CODE, uleb(1) + code_body([], body))
    return WASM_MAGIC + WASM_VERSION + type_sec + func_sec + export_sec + code


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly choose between several shapes including a minimal baseline
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.2:
        blob = minimal_module()
    else:
        blob = build_module(r, budget=1000)  # keep under fuzzer max 1024
    # Enforce upper bound 1024 (fuzzer clamps, but we ensure validity within the bound)
    if len(blob) > 1024:
        # As a last resort, return minimal valid
        blob = minimal_module()
    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces UTF-8 C strings intended for Wasm3 identifiers:
# - Module names for m3_SetModuleName
# - Exported function names for m3_FindFunction
# - Global names for m3_FindGlobal
#
# Strategy:
# - Prefer valid identifier-like names commonly used in Wasm toolchains (wasm-ld/clang/rustc/assemblyscript):
#   * ascii identifiers [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
#   * dotted module namespaces like env, wasi_snapshot_preview1, js, go, wasi:cli, wasi:filesystem
#   * function names including common exports: _start, _initialize, main, add, fib, memory.grow, abort
#   * global names: __heap_base, __data_end, __stack_pointer, __indirect_function_table, __stack_high, __stack_low
# - Include Unicode in some cases to exercise UTF-8 handling while remaining valid C-strings
# - Ensure null-terminated by Python bytes ending without embedded null manipulation (C side uses c_str())
# - Keep under 4096 bytes (we generate small strings)
#
# The fuzzer framework will reuse the same buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR across call sites, so
# we bias the selection towards names that are likely to exist in typical test modules.

COMMON_MODULES = [
    "env",
    "wasi_snapshot_preview1",
    "wasi_unstable",
    "wasi:cli",
    "wasi:filesystem",
    "wasi:random",
    "js",
    "go",
    "python",
    "assemblyscript",
]

COMMON_FUNCTIONS = [
    "_start",
    "_initialize",
    "main",
    "_main",
    "memcpy",
    "memmove",
    "memset",
    "abort",
    "__wasm_call_ctors",
    "__wasm_call_dtors",
    "_Z3addii",   # mangled C++ add(int,int)
    "add",
    "fib",
    "fact",
    "memory.grow",
    "memory.size",
    "__indirect_function_table",  # sometimes exported as a function/table name in some toolchains
]

COMMON_GLOBALS = [
    "__heap_base",
    "__data_end",
    "__stack_pointer",
    "__stack_high",
    "__stack_low",
    "_errno_location",
    "__memory_base",
    "__table_base",
]

UNICODE_WORDS = [
    "módulo",
    "функция",
    "函数",
    "関数",
    "함수",
    "फ़ंक्शन",
    "βeta",
    "π_calc",
    "名字",
]

# Assemble weighted pools for different call sites. Since we don't know which stub
# is being exercised at call time, we mix them with weights and also generate random identifiers.

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=24) -> str:
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest_len = rng.randint(min_len - 1 if min_len > 0 else 0, max_len - 1)
    rest_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(rest_len))
    return first + rest

def _rand_namespace(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # produce dotted/colon namespaces like wasi:cli/run or env.memory.grow
    parts = []
    n = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for i in range(n):
        base = _rand_ident(rng, 1, rng.randint(4, 12))
        parts.append(base)
    sep = rng.choice(['.', ':'])
    return sep.join(parts)

def _maybe_unicode(rng: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        uni = rng.choice(UNICODE_WORDS)
        # mix unicode as prefix/suffix to keep plausible identifier
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            return uni + "_" + base
        else:
            return base + "_" + uni
    return base

def _pick_candidate(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Weighted selection among modules, functions, globals, random idents, namespaces, unicode
    pools: List[str] = []
    # Add common items multiple times to bias selection
    pools += COMMON_MODULES * 3
    pools += COMMON_FUNCTIONS * 4
    pools += COMMON_GLOBALS * 4
    # Some compound names often seen
    pools += [
        "env._start",
        "env.abort",
        "wasi_snapshot_preview1.proc_exit",
        "wasi_snapshot_preview1.fd_write",
        "wasi_snapshot_preview1.fd_read",
        "wasi_snapshot_preview1.random_get",
        "js.memory.grow",
        "go.run",
    ] * 2
    # Occasionally create random identifiers or namespaces
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pools.append(_rand_ident(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pools.append(_rand_namespace(rng))
    choice = rng.choice(pools)
    return _maybe_unicode(rng, choice)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Produce between 1 and 3 concatenated C-strings separated by newlines or commas occasionally,
    # but since the stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR separately each time, we should return a single string.
    # Keep length small (< 256) and valid UTF-8
    s = _pick_candidate(rng)

    # Occasionally tweak case or add numeric suffix to broaden coverage
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.2:
        s = s.upper()
    elif roll < 0.4:
        s = s.lower()
    elif roll < 0.6:
        s = f"{s}{rng.randint(0, 9)}"

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(s.encode('utf-8')) > 4096:
        s = s[:512]

    # Return bytes; C++ fuzzer will interpret it as raw data for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and create a std::string
    return s.encode('utf-8')
